teaser: The five readers' views arrived as folds inside the long piece; now the reader picks the way in, with a default, and the finished article stays at the centre.
core_idea: The views the five readers make, the catalogue, the maps, the arc, the two-minute version and the deck, are good and badly delivered, stacked as folds inside the article; with the pane about the piece the reader picks a mode in one tap and sets a default per persona: headlines, infographic, two minutes, slides, what is new against what they have read, facts, relationships, vocabulary, and, through a model in their own browser, a view at their level; most modes are computed from existing views and the graph, deterministic and explainable, with no round trip to the publisher; and the finished article is kept whole at the centre because it has a beginning, a pacing, a surprise and a voice and is the one artefact that must make sense end to end, which a graph cannot.

nodes.label: The views worked, the delivery did not
nodes.summary: Five readers' views on five articles, delivered as folds inside the long piece, mixed with the thing they are an alternative to.

nodes.label: The reader picks the way in
nodes.summary: Headlines, infographic, two minutes, slides, what is new, facts, relationships, vocabulary, at my level, the whole article; one tap in the pane; a default per persona; the mode in the address.

nodes.label: Focus and time
nodes.summary: The reader's constraint is time and their need is focus; the unit of choice is the way in, not the article.

nodes.label: Deterministic first, a model second
nodes.summary: Most modes are projections of existing views and the graph, computed and explainable; a local model is for fitting the piece to the reader; nothing round-trips to the publisher.

nodes.label: The infographic is often the article
nodes.summary: The figures carry most of the story; a figure drawn for one reader through their own image-model key is a small step.

nodes.label: What is new
nodes.summary: The Historian's arc crossed with the reader's own records shows only what this article adds to what they have read; needs the vault.

nodes.label: The finished article stays at the centre
nodes.summary: A beginning, a sequence, a pacing, a surprise and a voice; the one artefact that has to make sense end to end, which a graph cannot.

nodes.label: What the graph loses
nodes.summary: Hyperlinked facts, right for provenance and zooming in, with no narrative and no author.

nodes.label: Phone, tablet, desktop, email
nodes.summary: On a phone the pane is a sheet and the default mode comes first; in email the newsletter is cut by the reader's default.

nodes.label: Not prose: the finished article
nodes.summary: The word made the article sound lesser than the graph beside it; from now on it is the finished article, or the narrative.

quotes.text: The views exist; the choice does not
the article is the one artefact that has to make sense in a coherent way, from end to end, and the graph is the one that has to be checkable.
quotes.why: The rule that keeps the article at the centre.

quotes.text: The modes are ways into the article for a reader with twenty seconds, two minutes or an hour.
quotes.why: What the modes are, and are not.
